newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's White Martins names new president.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's White Martins names new president.

text.p: The new president of Brazil's White Martins Produtos de Carbono SA on Thursday said he aimed to increase productivity and growth at South America's largest producer of industrial gases by taking advantage of the region's improved economic performance.

Earlier, White Martins said Ivan Ferreira Garcia, 54, a former vice president, had taken over as president, replacing Felix de Bulhoes, who held the post for 11 years. De Bulhoes will continue to serve as president of the company's administrative council.
"Our objective is to grow 10 percent a year," Garcia said. "The South American continent is going through a spectacular period. We are all seeing strong growth."

White Martins will invest $300 million a year during the next three years in its operations in Brazil and elsewhere in South America, with 70 percent going toward boosting growth and 30 percent aimed at increasing productivity.
The company, which is 69.3 percent owned by Praxair Inc, a U.S. industrial gas concern, operates in 10 South American countries.
It aims to increase sales outside of Brazil to 25 percent of the total by the year 2000 from a current 18 percent, said Garcia, who spoke at a luncheon where the company announced his appointment.

This year's investments include two new $25 million gas-production plants with daily capacities of 150 tonnes. One of them, located in Pisco, 150 miles (240 km) south of Lima, is due to come on line in October or November. The other, located in the southern Colombian city of Cali, is expected to start operations in August.
Garcia said the company had just concluded two contracts to build oxygen plants in Chile and Argentina, which would come on line in the second half of next year.

Under the deals, White Martins will invest $20 million in a 100-tonne-a-day plant near Santiago serving Chilean steelmaker Siderurgica Aza SA and $35 million in a 400-tonne-a-day plant near Buenos Aires serving Argentine steelmaker Siderca SACI.

Garcia said White Martins was also following closely the privatization process of Venezuelan steel company Sidor, which could result in an investment opportunity of about $20 million in a new oxygen plant.
